findings.obligation: The feature's own declared Equality says two rails that differ only in row wrapping, tint, glyph, token name or SOURCE ORDER are the same rail, and an acceptance assertion reads outcome, state and required fields rather than incidental ordering unless the authority promises it. The order the destinations are offered in is the law of the nav-quick-actions lane, which this Request kept there ('Then the left nav offers these destinations in this order', passing in run 2).
findings.observation: The step collects the offered pairs in document order into a Vec and asserts list equality, and its failure text reads 'the left nav must offer this operator [...], in that order'. The measured RED message of both P2 rows therefore carries an order claim this feature does not promise: it distinguishes two rails the declared equality calls equal, and it duplicates another lane's law, so a future reorder of the partial would fail a P2 row for a cause that is not P2. The shipped icon-rail support does the opposite and deliberately sorts both sides before comparing (feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:887).
findings.remediation: Compare the offered word-and-href pairs as a SET - sort both sides before the equality, as support/steps feature_nav_icon_rail::assert_rail_offers already does - and drop 'in that order' from the message. Keep the exact-membership equality and the table as written; leave the order law to nav-quick-actions.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/ui-nav-polish.feature:179-189 (Scenario Outline 'A page with nothing to scroll leaves the nav where it has always been' and its stated RED-trigger), and the P3 row of docs/feature/ui-nav-polish/acceptance.md
findings.obligation: An oracle's stated RED-trigger and its acceptance row must match the measured state of the shipped build, so the craft step can tell a row that is owed a change from a row that pins today's behaviour.
findings.observation: The comment says 'The other half of the law: nothing about a short page changes' and the acceptance P3 row says 'On a page with nothing to scroll the nav is in view exactly as it has always been'. Measured in run 1, the open-nav short-page row FAILS today: 'with the page scrolled 0 px down, the left nav runs from 0 to 769 in a window 757 px tall' - on /account/settings the open rail already overflows the window by 12 px. The folded short-page row passes. So one of the two rows is a RED row the fix must turn green, not a preservation guard, and both narratives mis-describe the shipped build.
findings.remediation: Reword the scenario comment and the acceptance P3 row to state the measured fact - on a page with nothing to scroll the open rail is 769 px in a 757 px window today, the folded one already fits - and keep the assertion exactly as it is; height:100vh with overflow-y:auto makes both rows green. No assertion change is needed.

Run 2, changed-by-design lane. ARGV: scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=nav-quick-actions cargo test -p foundry-acceptance". EXIT=101. stdout: 1 feature, 9 scenarios (7 passed, 2 failed), 67 steps (65 passed, 2 failed). The two failures are the two migrated rights rows - 'A member with no rights beyond her workspace opens the three places her rights open' and 'An instance super-admin who administers no workspace opens the same three places' - both on 'Then the left nav offers these destinations in this order', which is P2 semantic RED. The migration also replaced that lane's '/teams marks Home' outline row with '/account/settings keeps Home as the one marked item', which passes, so the two authorities no longer contradict: ui-nav-polish owns which item is marked on the three moved families, nav-quick-actions keeps the order law and the complement page.

Oracle quality, judged on the bytes. Driving port: every mark-and-offer scenario is one authenticated HTTP GET of the running application with a real session cookie through support::harness (establish_session/get_with_cookie), and the three geometry promises are the same GETs in the real browser the @needs-browser lane drives; no step imports a production module other than the harness, no step asserts a private field, a mock call or a class name. Port treatment matches the Architecture of Reference: driven-internal Postgres is REAL per scenario (@real-io) as the walking-skeleton-grade rail lanes already run it, and no fake stands where the promised failure could hide. Anti-vacuity is built into each row rather than assumed: the rights grant is written and read back with rows_affected (a silently failed grant would otherwise turn an admin row into a second copy of the no-rights row), the long page asserts doc > 1.5x window before scrolling and scrollY > 0 after, the short page asserts doc <= 1.1x window, the fold is a real press of .sidebar__brand button[aria-expanded] plus a re-read proving the document took the mark, the phone rows assert the laid-out width is 390 +/- 1 px before measuring, and the quiet rows panic if no neighbour link or no control is present to compare with. The expected sets are written out in the feature table and every offered href is then re-opened with the SAME cookie, so the rail is never compared against itself. Expected values come from the promises (168.8 px = 844/5, 44 px thumb, 'no border their neighbours lack'), not from the code under test.

Closure, both directions. Every promise has at least one falsifiable observation that failed for its own reason this run: P1 the mark outline over all six page families plus the two no-owner rows, with 'and nothing else' read as a set equality over .sidebar a.sidebar__item[aria-current=page] (which also catches a second mark in the lower group, the nearest wrong implementation); P2 the four-row closed rights domain on ONE page, the offered-set equality, the every-offered-href-opens walk and the typed-address 404 row; P3 both geometries long and short; P4 four readings at the 390x844 device incl. folded and no-script; P5 both palettes, the no-script bound, and the two still-acts rows. The reverse direction holds too: every observation in the new lane maps to P1-P5 or to the shipped rail law it must not break (invisible-and-focusable, 44 px, no sideways slide). Examiner expectations: E1 covered by the set equality; E2 by /team/backend/members with the remaining sub pages left explicitly unobserved; E3 by the workspace-admin rows plus the href walk; E4 by document absence at desk width plus the changed icon-rail lane's exact rights-derived set in the folded geometry and with no scripting; E5 by a real scroll and the measured rail box, not a declared style value; E6/E7 by the measured bar against the measured screen with every member visible, focusable and 44 px, and the shipped icon-rail phone rows already drive 320, 390 and 480 px; E8 by a resolved painted-fill comparison with a neighbour link in both palettes; E9 by the two press rows.

No judgment was fabricated and no producer-owned judgment was reused; the four questions were resolved locally against the oracle bytes and the measured run, and that limitation is retained here. Timing: no measurement taken and none owed - no test in the reviewed oracle is at or above half its budget by any supplied receipt, the lane is the repository's @needs-browser acceptance lane rather than a unit suite, and no derogation is claimed or granted.

RED is honest and committed. The oracle commit e0033b7 touches no production byte (only the acceptance crate, its two registration lines and the docs), so no stub, placeholder or pass-bridge manufactures the RED. The lane carries no @pending, @manual, #[ignore] or should_panic, and the runner is built with fail_on_skipped, so an unwired step fails instead of skipping - the 15 failures are therefore observations that ran. The three geometry promises are @needs-browser, which the default fast lane excludes; this review ran them by tag, so the evidence names the lane that actually observed them rather than a gate that would be green on a host with no Docker. Two obligations are deferred by design rather than missing here: T1 (the mark-comes-from-the-carrier rule beside the shipped rail-member law) has its locator in xtask/src/check_arch.rs, which the packet lists as a read-only Extend target of the craft step, so it is a completion obligation and not oracle bytes; and the B1 row (the rights lookup failing mid-render) is declared NotTested with owner solution-architect because no public surface or declared seam makes that lookup fail, its observable consequence being covered by the rights rows.

Limits retained, with the reason each is acceptable rather than hidden. (1) P4 promises the one-fifth bound over the band 390 px to 480 px, and the new lane measures it at 390 only. The shipped stylesheet governs that whole band from ONE rule block, @media (max-width: 480px) (the only phone breakpoint in the file, inclusive of 480), and a wider viewport wraps the same members into fewer rows, so the bound at 480 cannot exceed the bound at 390 under the designed mechanism; the other half of P4 - every destination stays one press away at 480 px and below - is already driven at 320, 390 and 480 px by the shipped nav-collapse-icon-rail phone rows, whose owed set this Request made rights-derived. No finding, but the 480 px height reading itself stays unobserved and open_mobile_session_sized(480, 844) would construct it. (2) Widths under 390 px are an authorized product exclusion (user decision 2026-11-20) recorded as Unknown with owner product-owner; the lane asserts at every driven width that nothing is hidden to make the bar fit. (3) Sub pages under the invite and tokens families are unvisited; one deeper page is observed (/team/backend/members) and the design routes all renders of each module through one carrier helper. (4) Hover and phone-width readings of the quiet lower group are unobserved; no promise distinguishes them.

diagnostic: Accepted. The public oracle for S1 is constructible, independent and complete over the declared obligations, and the missing behaviour shows semantic RED. Run 1 (FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=ui-nav-polish, exit 101) gave 26 scenarios, 11 passed and 15 failed, 161 steps, 0 parsing errors and 0 hook errors: four P1 rows read [Home] where the owner item is owed, two P2 rows are offered the two admin links they must not see, three P3 rows measure the rail outside the window (-4367 to 757 and -3467 to 757 after a real scroll, and 0 to 769 in a 757 px window on the short page), three P4 rows measure 277 px of 844 and 259 px of 701 against the 168.8 and 140.2 px a fifth allows, and three P5 rows read Sign out at fill rgb(36,38,37) with a 1 px border beside neighbour links on the rail surface. Every failure is a business observation with its WHAT, WHY and FIX; none is an import, fixture, collection or startup failure. Run 2 (nav-quick-actions, exit 101) gave the two migrated rights rows RED and removed the contradicting Home-on-/teams row, so two authorities no longer disagree. The oracle drives the real public port only, writes its expected sets out instead of reading them off the rail, re-opens every offered href with the same cookie, and refuses to measure a page, a fold or a width it did not first prove. Two findings, both non-blocking and both owned by the oracle: the offered-set step asserts document ORDER, which this feature's own equality calls incidental and another lane already owns; and the short-page row's narrative says nothing changes on a short page while the measurement shows the open rail 12 px over the window today. Neither prevents craft. Limits retained: the nav-collapse-icon-rail lane was selected and queued but never ran, because a concurrent session held the shared test lock with a cargo-mutants sweep, so its exit is unobserved and its migration is judged on its bytes; the one-fifth bound is read at 390 px only, with the 480 px edge governed by the same single stylesheet breakpoint and its reachability half already driven at 320, 390 and 480 px by the shipped phone rows; Jev was unavailable (no API key), so every judgment here is local. Completion still owes: production GREEN on all 15 rows, the T1 check-arch obligation in xtask, and one run of the icon-rail lane.
